clue.text: Research area of a politician chasing work in America

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so the politician follows the work

parts.note: labor is the American spelling of labour, meaning work
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A news item about where a politician pursues employment in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling drops the U of the British word for work; 'chasing' puts the politician behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a room or building set aside for scientific research and experiments.

clue.text: Order will come after leader's first rounded projection

indicators.note: the order is placed following the leader's opening letter
the first of the word leader is its opening letter only

parts.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: An instruction that a command will follow the head person's initial one.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour; it goes after L, the opening letter of 'leader'.
explanation.definitionFit: An earlobe or a lobe of the lung or brain is a rounded part sticking out from something larger.

clue.text: Travelling people's place for sleeping — nothing posh at home

parts.note: a bed is where one sleeps
O looks like zero, nothing
U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A wanderer's sleeping spot is described as having nothing fancy about the house.
explanation.walkthrough: U for 'posh' comes from the old U and non-U division of upper-class and other speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bedouin are nomadic Arab peoples of the desert, moving their camps from place to place.

clue.text: Where working hands must be on the move constantly

definitions.text: Where working hands must be on the move
definitions.meaning: the hands of a clock that works keep travelling around its face

explanation.surface: A remark that busy labourers must keep moving all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working hands' look like labourers, but they are the hands of a clock that is going.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the clock's hands making full circuits, hence continuously, at all hours.

clue.text: Film shot on river with ducks needing time to become established

parts.note: a take is one filmed shot of a scene
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so two ducks are two Os

explanation.surface: A film scene shot on a river with ducks takes time to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a zero score in cricket, giving O; ducks plural give OO.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant whose roots grow into the soil becomes settled, so the phrase means to become firmly settled.

clue.text: Missing starter, characteristic area dish with curry

indicators.note: missing its starter means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic

explanation.surface: A restaurant review: no first course, but a typical regional curry dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing starter' looks like a menu comment but takes the T off TRAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian side dish of yoghurt with cucumber or mint, served alongside spicy food.

clue.text: Did the butterfly show on the outside in the morning?

indicators.note: only the outside letters of the word show are taken

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, in the morning

explanation.surface: A question about whether a butterfly appeared outdoors early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The butterfly is a swimming stroke, not an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing the butterfly means performing that swimming stroke, so in the past tense the swimmer moved through water.

clue.text: Bird dog's happy to do this?

definitions.meaning: a small songbird with a long flicking tail
a pleased dog shakes its rear end from side to side

explanation.surface: Asking whether a bird-dog shows pleasure this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird dog' reads as a gundog, but splits into a definition and a cryptic hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipit-like songbird is named for its bobbing tail, and a cheerful hound does exactly that.

clue.text: Warm to Kent after moving — Cranbrook perhaps

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone warming to the county of Kent after relocating to Cranbrook.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; Cranbrook is a small town in it with a long history of trading.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranbrook is an example of a town that historically held a regular trading market.

clue.text: Excited lad coming into dollar fortune such as this

indicators.note: the shuffled letters enter the middle of the dollar word

parts.note: a buck is slang for a dollar

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A thrilled boy comes into money, yet the clue hints this luck is unfortunate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' reads as the lad's mood but scrambles his letters to ADL; 'coming into' sets them inside the dollar slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Misfortune is a kind of fortune, so an unlucky turn of events fits 'fortune such as this'.

clue.text: Number, for example, found in Bury?

indicators.note: the example abbreviation is placed inside the burial word

parts.note: to inter is to bury
EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Suggesting a number, say, is found in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town in north-west England, but here the verb to bury, INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number without fractions is called by this mathematical term.

clue.text: Changing group for the shortest round trip

parts.note: turning is changing, as leaves turn colour
a circle is a group of people, such as a circle of friends

explanation.surface: A changing set of people chosen to make the briefest return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle's turning circle is the smallest loop in which it can turn completely around.

clue.text: Less than the cost of transporting part of plane?

parts.note: under means less than, as in under ten pounds
carriage is the charge for transporting goods

explanation.surface: A question about paying below the delivery charge for shipping a piece of an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheels and supporting frame beneath an aircraft are its landing gear, this structure.

clue.text: Copper that's invested in dodgy pet deals took a risk

indicators.note: being invested in means being put inside, here inside the reworked letters
dodgy suggests the letters are shady and rearranged

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer who put money into shady pet deals gambled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is CU, set inside SPELATED, the rearrangement of PET DEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: To speculate is to gamble on investments in hope of gain, so the past tense means gambled.

clue.text: Circle inscribed in the name alongside slate monument

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, the same as to slate

indicators.note: inscribed in means written inside, so the ring goes inside the following letters

parts.note: taken as written
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A ring carved into a name next to a stone tablet on a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slate' looks like the stone but is the verb meaning criticise, PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon can be a building honouring the illustrious dead, such as the one in Paris, a memorial.

clue.text: Flutter around unfriendly accommodation for the military

indicators.note: the wager word goes around the outside of the unfriendly word

parts.note: a flutter is a small bet
ill can mean hostile, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A small gamble on hostile lodgings for soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is British slang for a small bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers' lodging in a private house or other quarters is this term for a place to sleep.

clue.text: Attacks group working to support drink

indicators.note: in a down answer, a supporting piece sits beneath the one it holds up

parts.note: a set is a group
to sup is to drink
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A gang at work assaults people to pay for drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To set upon someone is an idiom meaning to assault or attack them.

clue.text: Sort of bag used for eggs

definitions.meaning: a small strapless handbag held in the hand
the word for a set of eggs laid together

explanation.definitionFit: A strapless evening handbag and a batch of eggs laid at one time share this one word.

clue.text: University note victory and good economic recovery

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is a note added to a letter
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A university message celebrates a win and a healthy rebound in the economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests a musical note, but here it is PS, a postscript.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn in economic activity after a slump is described as a rise or upward swing.

clue.text: Boundary that secures advantage in hospital dispute

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so these outer letters grip the advantage word

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or dispute
an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: A dividing line that gains the upper hand in a hospital quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of shrubs planted along a field's edge marks its limit in the countryside.

clue.text: Snake gets right under nipper's toy!

indicators.note: in a down answer, the right letter sits below the toy

parts.note: a nipper is a small child, whose toy might be a rattle

explanation.surface: A snake ends up beneath a little child's plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: Nipper is British slang for a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake is informally called by this shortened name, from the sound its tail makes.

clue.text: Prancing horse on stilts came a cropper after a flutter

definitions.text: came a cropper after a flutter

indicators.note: prancing letters jump around into a new order

explanation.surface: A prancing horse on stilts fell over after a wobble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came a cropper' is British for suffered a failure, and a flutter is a small bet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means lost everything, usually through gambling, so it suits a bettor ruined by a wager.

clue.text: Mistake made by English bishop over gold

indicators.note: in a down answer, the earlier pieces sit above the gold

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An English bishop gets it wrong about some gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder or slip is a fault, the same as getting something wrong.

clue.text: Tool for cutting a nap with no end of ballyhoo

indicators.note: no means the named letter is left out of the nap word

parts.note: a doze is a short nap

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A cutting tool for a short sleep without the fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes O, the final letter of 'ballyhoo', from DOZE.
explanation.definitionFit: This woodworking implement has an arched blade set at right angles to its handle, used to shape timber.

clue.text: One ponders, having weak King with Queen

parts.note: a thin argument or drink is weak
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A feeble king and his queen sit pondering.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reflects deeply, like a philosopher, is a person who ponders.

clue.text: Chose to cross line blind drunk

indicators.note: the choosing word straddles the line, holding it inside

parts.note: picked means chose

explanation.surface: A drunk staggers over a line chosen for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is slang for very intoxicated, as if preserved in alcohol.

clue.text: Understands one's love for these pets

indicators.note: for means one letter is exchanged, the love letter standing in for the one

parts.note: digs is slang for understands or likes
one is the Roman numeral I
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone who gets what one loves about these animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Hounds, spaniels and terriers are kept as household pets, the commonest kind.

clue.text: Growth of teenager trained by soldiers

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: trained letters are reshaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The development of a young person drilled by troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' suggests adolescence, but it is the definition; 'trained' rearranges the young person's letters to ANGETREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus tree is something that grows, so it is a fair example of a growth.
